statement: For every epsilon>0, delta in (0,1/2), and hidden-state cap D>=2, there is a finite-bit, full-support binary order-one predictor q and two stationary HMMs with at most two states such that R_P0(q)<=epsilon/2, R_P1(q)>=2epsilon, and the complete infinite observation-path laws have TV p chosen so (1-p)(1-delta)>delta. Therefore no randomized post-hoc certifier for q can be both (epsilon,delta)-complete and sound, even when it sees the entire infinite raw path.
interface: One stationary raw path; sequential observation access; no reset, hidden-state, conditional-entry, dictionary, mixing, context-floor, or gap oracle; q is supplied before path; certificate is a finite stopping PASS/NO decision.
assumptions: Stationary HMM class includes reducible transition matrices
costs: q uses O(L+B) dyadic coefficient bits; B=O(1+epsilon/p), L=O(log(1/epsilon)) for small epsilon; P1 stationary weight p has O(log denominator(p)) bits; lower bound holds against unbounded computation and full-path retention.
limitations: This is a post-hoc certificate impossibility for a supplied q, not a lower bound against every data-dependent learner. Exact infinite-path indistinguishability uses reducibility.

statement: For the same q and any almost-surely finite adaptive certifier that is complete on P0, there exists an irreducible two-state stationary Markov HMM P_a with the same stationary state-1 mass p, no lower bound on its mixing rate, R_Pa(q)>=2epsilon, and an all-zero prefix overlap large enough to force false certification probability above delta. Hence no certificate can be uniformly complete and sound over irreducible chains without a supplied rate bound.
interface: Same as preceding claim; certifier may use all raw symbols and internal randomness, but must stop almost surely on each low-risk instance.
assumptions: No positive lower bound on the transition or mixing rate
Candidate q is fixed and supplied
Uniform completeness and soundness over the class
costs: For finite horizon T, choose a=2^-M with M large enough that (1-p)(1-a)^(T-1) preserves the testing overlap; coefficient length M is O(log T plus confidence margin), and b=a(1-p)/p has O(M+log denominator(p)) bits. The exposure waiting time from state 0 is geometric with mean 1/a.
limitations: Each fixed irreducible alternative is eventually distinguishable with unlimited time. The theorem rules out uniform finite stopping without a rate, not eventual pointwise discrimination.

statement: Whether every data-dependent predictor learner lacks a finite-time high-confidence guarantee for stationary-history predictive KL under the same finite-state HMM class is not established. The proved result concerns certification of a fixed supplied predictor.
reason_unknown: Robust or universal predictors may avoid the bad q; existing literature establishes no-gap expected-risk prediction for fully observed Markov chains.
